thread:
lee.devex: heads-up: customer reported rerank pipeline broken after they upgraded Ruby SDK. Seems like embedding shape mismatch between Ruby and Go SDKs when using batching-helper + streaming response.

lee.devex: quick repro: sample-app calls rerank with batch_size=2 -> server streams NDJSON chunks with a top-level 'vectors' field per-chunk. Go client concatenates arrays into NxD correctly. Ruby client flattens into a single list and then splits by 'vector_count' field which is absent in stream meta, so resulting per-vector length is wrong.

lee.devex: example stream (simplified):
```json
{"meta": {"pad_to": 512}, "vectors": [[...512 floats...],[...512 floats...]]}
{"meta": {"pad_to": 512}, "vectors": [[...512 floats...]]}
```

anya-ruby: thanks. Ruby was relying on a legacy "vector_count" header in the final payload to know how to split. With streaming we get chunked vectors and Ruby's old parser assumed a single flat array. That's a bug on our side but surprising the Go SDK handled stream-of-arrays fine.

tom-go: Go's client treats each chunk as a list of vectors and appends per-chunk. We also validate per-vector length against meta.pad_to if present. Does Ruby not validate?

anya-ruby: not reliably. We added a shim to support older unary responses where server returned a single flattened array and a count. But streaming semantics changed and the shim is now counterproductive.

sasha-ml: possible contributing factor: auth retry can merge chunks incorrectly in the Ruby HTTP client; streaming replays previously-read bytes and Ruby ends up with an extra nil/trim at chunk boundaries. Can someone reproduce with auth-flap toggled on?

lee.devex: I ran an experiment: reproduce with sample-app env var `FORCE_AUTH_FLAP=true` -> Ruby returns vectors of length 511 occasionally (pad_to=512), Go always returns 512. So two problems: (1) Ruby's splitter logic, (2) retry/stream reassembly bug that drops a float at a chunk boundary.

ci-bot: Created issue #4123: "rerank streaming: sdk parity - ruby flattening + retry chunk trim" assigned to @anya-ruby and @tom-go.

anya-ruby: plan: remove legacy flattening shim, update streaming parser to accept chunked vectors, add per-vector validation (raise + retry on mismatch). I'll open a draft PR today.

tom-go: I'll add cross-SDK integration test in CI that runs both Go and Ruby sample apps against a streaming mock that simulates auth-flap and chunk-splits floats at random boundaries. If either client reports a shape mismatch, CI should fail.

sasha-ml: longer-term runtime change: include an explicit "vectors_in_chunk" and per-vector checksum in streaming meta to make SDKs robust. Also add a top-level response-field name that is consistent (we should standardize on "embeddings" instead of both "vectors" and "embeddings").

lee.devex: customer workaround: bump sample-app to use Go SDK or set sample-app to unary mode (no stream). I've communicated ETA ~48h for SDK patch.

anya-ruby: also adding a quick client-side heuristic: if the parser detects per-vector length mismatch vs pad_to, it will re-request the whole batch (idempotent) up to 2 attempts and emit telemetry "embed.dim_mismatch". That should reduce customer impact while runtime checksum lands.

helen: note for onboarding docs: document streaming vs unary expectations and mention pad_to semantics. I'll add a small FAQ entry about "why did my Ruby SDK get 511-length vectors".

lee.devex: thanks all. filing release note: "Fix(ruby): streaming embeddings parser removed legacy flattening path; added dim-check + retry. Add parity CI for streaming embedding responses."

ci-bot: CI job #2156 queued for PR anya/ruby#fix-stream-parser.

lee.devex: resolving thread, will reopen if further regressions show up.
